faq: Is a reset link safe to email?
Yes, when done properly. Each link is random, single-use and short-lived. We also avoid saying whether an email exists on your site, so strangers cannot probe for accounts.
Can people reset by text message instead?
This service covers email. Text resets need an SMS provider and extra care because numbers can be hijacked. If you need it, tell us and we quote it separately.
What if my emails land in spam?
We check the sender name, template and basic email settings such as SPF and DKIM with you. We cannot control every inbox, but a correct setup improves the chance of arrival.
Can you improve a reset flow that already exists?
Yes. Share the project, and we test the current flow for weak points such as links that never expire. We then fix them without changing your user records.

desc:
A password reset and account recovery flow lets users who forgot their password get back in on their own, safely. Ecom Swift LLC builds the forgot-password page, the reset email and the new-password screen inside your own app.

## What is a password reset flow?

A password reset flow is the sequence a user follows after forgetting their password. They enter their email, receive a link, open a secure page, choose a new password and return to the app. Each step must be easy for the real owner and awkward for anyone else.

It sounds routine, yet it is one of the most sensitive paths in a product. Whoever completes it controls the account.

## Why forgotten passwords deserve careful design

Forgotten passwords are among the most common reasons people write to support. If the flow is missing, every case becomes a ticket. If the flow is careless, it becomes an attack route: guessable links, links that never expire, or a page that tells strangers which emails have accounts.

A weak flow also hurts the honest majority. A reset email that arrives late, looks like spam or leads to a confusing page makes the user try again, and then give up.

## How a good flow reduces support and protects accounts

The mechanism has two sides. For users, a clear path means they solve the problem in a minute and return to work, so fewer tickets reach your team. For security, the design choices close the gaps attackers look for.

Single-use links mean a forwarded or leaked email cannot be replayed. Expiry limits the window of risk. A neutral response, the same message whether or not the email exists, stops people from checking who is a customer. Ending older sessions after a reset removes anyone who was already signed in on a stolen device.

## What a great reset flow includes

- A forgot-password page that asks only for an email address.
- A reset email with one clear button and a plain explanation.
- A link that works once and expires after a set time.
- A new-password page with live checks and a visible requirements list.
- The same on-screen message whether the email exists or not.
- Limits on how often reset requests can be made for one address or device.
- A confirmation email after the password changes.
- Other sessions signed out when the reset completes.
- A check against commonly used passwords.
- Reset activity that admins can see when helping a customer.

## What we do

We review how your login works today, then build or tidy each step. We create the request page, the token handling on the server, the email templates and the new-password screen, and we match them to your design.

Testing is a real part of the work. We try an expired link, a reused link, a request for an unknown email and many requests in a row, and we check that each one behaves safely. We also check what the reset does to existing sessions.

The Basic package delivers the working flow with an expiring one-use link. Standard adds branded emails, request limits, the neutral response, sign-out of other sessions and the tests above. Premium adds a password strength guide, a common-password check, change-alert emails, admin visibility of reset activity and handover notes.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Show the same message for known and unknown emails.
- Make links single-use and short-lived.
- Email the owner when the password has changed.
- Sign out other devices after a reset.
- Keep the reset page in the same look as your app so it feels trustworthy.

**Avoid:**
- Emailing a new password in plain text.
- Security questions with answers that are easy to find online.
- Links that stay valid for days.
- Error messages that confirm which emails are registered.
- Reset emails that ask users to log in through a link to a different site.

## Who this is for

This service suits a new app with a login but no way back in. It also suits a product where support keeps resetting passwords by hand, and a team that suspects its current flow is too generous with strangers. A business that is moving to a new login system and wants the recovery step to be clean will also benefit.

## What we need from you

Send your brand details, the email service you use and a short description of how users sign in today. We need collaborator or developer access to the project and a staging environment, plus a test mailbox if you have one. We never ask for passwords. Tell us if you want a reset by text message to be considered, as that is a separate decision with its own trade-offs.
